title: Peak water has passed: summer runoff from the Sorne glacier catchment to 2060

speaker.name: Léa Montandon
speaker.about: final-year PhD candidate in mountain hydrology presenting a conference paper; answers four setup questions, adds no extra files, and asks for one subject to be left alone

interview: No extra files. Two things the slides don't say: the model runs at a daily time step, and all 1,800 runs took about 9 hours on the university cluster.
Debris cover is the biggest caveat. My guess is that including it would soften the August decline by 2 to 4 percentage points, but I have not run it yet; that is the next paper.
The canton's water office and the reservoir operator have seen the results, and the operator is using them in its 2027 concession review. I cannot share the operator's own inflow data.
Please don't get into the 2015 projection, which was my supervisor's and more optimistic. I'd rather not be asked about it or compare with it here.

audience.name: Henrik Solberg

asks: Are the 50 retained parameter sets weighted equally, or by their score, when the 10-90% range is computed? The slides don't say. And is the 0.82 validation NSE on daily flows?
Slide 2 says August runoff falls 38% by the 2050s, but slide 11 says annual runoff falls only 9% for the same decade and scenario. These look like they contradict each other. Which number is right?

asks.q: The four shares on slide 13 (GCM 46%, scenario 31%, parameters 17%, internal 6%) add up to exactly 100%. Where are the interaction terms, for example GCM x scenario? Were they dropped, or folded into the main effects?

asks.q: slide 9 figure 2 what is annual runoff 2040 exact value from the graph pls

asks: slide 5 formula if glacier is 6 degree up one day how much ice melt that day

replies.answer: About 13 GWh a year less summer generation at Brenay: 12 hm³ less water over a 480 m head at roughly 85% efficiency. That is my own estimate, not the operator's figure.
Interactions are not shown separately. GCM × scenario is about 5% of the variance and I counted it under GCM; the other interactions are each under 1%. The full table is in the preprint.
The median in 2040 is about 1,410 mm a year, against 1,590 mm at the peak in 2019. The 10–90% range in 2040 is 1,290 to 1,500 mm.
